title: fix: hide inline image controls on mobile
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: download and copy icons remain permanently visible over chat images on mobile.

## User Impact

Mobile image previews are unobstructed. Tapping an image still opens the existing lightbox, including its download control. Desktop controls retain hover and keyboard-focus behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing non-hover/coarse-pointer media rule forced the overlay on. Hide that overlay instead, without changing the image or lightbox components. This follows input capability rather than viewport width, so touch-first tablets are covered too.

Contributor credit: Hannes supplied the request and UX direction.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e753f136-8e7d-4800-8269-4f5380fd6e64)

## Evidence

- Regression fails on the original mobile visibility rule and passes with the fix. Existing real-Chromium/mock-Gateway E2E scenarios cover mobile tap-to-lightbox and repeated original-byte downloads, desktop hover/focus, and failed-download recovery: **2/2 passed**.
- `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/managed-image-actions.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **22.16 seconds** runner wall time; **3.66 seconds** test time. Hosted CI seconds: not yet available. The existing suite is extended; no new app boots or tests are added.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, focused stylelint/oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent review: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Simplification: one CSS declaration replaces the persistent-overlay override (production +1/-2 lines); the existing E2E flow now downloads through the lightbox on mobile (test +43/-26).
- Captures use synthetic content in the actual Control UI at a 390×844 touch viewport. Browser emulation, not physical-device proof.
